confirmed.prod_impact: Production (Railway auto-deploys main) serves PEDR search with NO per-layer diagnostics and NO `degraded` flag. Concretely on main today: (1) `from app.services.pedr import LayerDiagnostic` raises ImportError — the symbol is absent from the package import block (app/services/pedr/__init__.py:76-86) and `__all__` (lines 198-206), and the class itself is absent from app/services/pedr/search_orchestrator.py (PEDRMetadata at :171-187 has no `layer_diagnostics`/`degraded` fields). (2) When a retrieval layer fails (lexical :663, semantic :688, graph :745 — all `logger.warning` and continue), the orchestrator returns partial results that are indistinguishable from a complete response to API clients; the pre-deletion contract exposed `metadata.degraded=True` plus per-layer `status/error/error_type`. (3) The API no longer emits `pedr.layer_completed` / `pedr.layer_failed` SSE events (only PEDR_SEARCH_COMPLETED at app/api/v1/pedr_search.py:236), while the frontend MissionActivityFeed.tsx:102-103,200 and types/mission-events.ts:16-17 still listen for them — dead listeners, so the Mission Operations Center never shows layer failures. (4) The public response schema lost `PEDRLayerDiagnostic`, `PEDRLayerStatus`, `layer_diagnostics`, `degraded` (removed from app/schemas/pedr_search.py in aeb61bd). Data served is not wrong (results from healthy layers are still correct and project-scoped), and no security regression — but the T33.1 "degraded flag in responses / per-layer diagnostics" feature is silently gone in prod, and search-quality incidents (e.g. Qdrant outage → semantic layer down) are now invisible to clients and the console UI. confirmed.refuter_reasoning: I tried to refute the claim on the three permitted grounds and failed on all of them. (a) Moved: the name appears zero times in the post-commit __init__.py and zero times in the post-commit search_orchestrator.py, so there is no relocated import or alias. (b) Re-expressed equivalently: there is no Python construct that re-expresses a public re-export; either the name is bound in the package namespace and listed in __all__ or it is not. (c) Ruff autofix: ruff's isort (I) only reorders and splits import blocks — visible in the diff as the alphabetical reordering and the `EntityType as ...` splits — and F401 explicitly treats any name present in `__all__` as used, so ruff could not have removed `LayerDiagnostic` (or the 8 exception names) from either the import or `__all__`. The removal is therefore a hand/LLM edit riding inside a commit labeled "style", and it is the mechanically necessary companion to the deletion of `class LayerDiagnostic` from search_orchestrator.py (otherwise the package import itself would have raised ImportError at startup). The observable difference is real and binary: `from app.services.pedr import LayerDiagnostic` works at 8b049eda4b and raises ImportError at d592c92. The claim's restore guidance is correct and necessary: re-adding the class alone leaves the package path broken. I rated severity low rather than higher because this specific item has no runtime consumers via the package path and carries no damage independent of the already-confirmed class deletion; it is a completeness requirement for the restore, not a separate outage vector.

confirmed.prod_impact: Production (Railway auto-deploys main; d592c92 is an ancestor of main) no longer materializes implicit PEDR graph edges when a document is ingested. Before d592c92, every successful process_document call ran EdgeMaterializationService.materialize_implicit_edges(mode="incremental", project_id=...) and wrote document->project (belongs_to), project->document (contains), document->chunk (contains) and chunk->document (part_of) rows into graph_edges. On main today the only remaining writer of those implicit edges is the manual CLI `python -m app.cli.materialize_edges` (app/cli/materialize_edges.py) — there is no scheduled job, Procfile/railway hook, or API route that invokes it. graph_edges is read by the PEDR graph layer (app/services/pedr/graph_layer.py:332-337, graph_rag.py:269-272), which is consumed by the /pedr search path (app/api/v1/pedr_search.py, search_orchestrator.py, rag_service.py) for graph-enhanced expansion/re-ranking (Sprint 37 T37.4 measured graph re-ranking 4/12 queries). Net effect: newly ingested documents and their chunks are invisible to graph-enhanced search/RAG expansion until someone manually runs the CLI; the graph silently goes stale with every upload. The /health graph_edges edge_type counts (app/api/v1/health.py:126) also stop growing. The ingestion API response also lost stages.edges_materialized and metrics.edge_materialization_duration_seconds (contract change for any client reading them). No data is corrupted and no security regression — this is a feature silently gone (T37.3 deliverable un-shipped), so severity=high. Note also the CI-1 commit (6a3c514, 2026-08-20) quarantined all 7 tests in tests/test_ingestion_edge_materialization.py with reasons asserting a "contract change"/"retired incremental-call contract" — the quarantine hid the regression instead of flagging it; those tests are the exact coverage that would have caught the loss and should be un-quarantined once the block is restored.

confirmed.prod_impact: Stage 6 (incremental graph-edge materialization, T37.3) has been silently absent from the ingestion pipeline in production since d592c92 (2026-03-13), and Railway auto-deploys main. Consequences: (1) No document ingested in the last ~6 months has had its implicit graph edges (contains/belongs_to/part_of/references/derived_from/co_occurs/topic_similar) written to graph_edges, because the only other writer is the manual CLI app/cli/materialize_edges.py, which is not run by the Railway start command (railway.json:7 runs only `alembic upgrade head && uvicorn`) or any documented runbook. (2) PEDR search with enable_graph=true (app/api/v1/pedr_search.py:149, search_orchestrator.py graph layer) and RAG include_graph_context=true (rag_service.py:230 via graph_rag.py) do graph expansion over a stale edge set that omits all recent documents, so graph re-ranking/context silently ignores new content; GET /graph/stats (health.py:126) under-reports edge counts. (3) The ingestion result no longer carries stages.edges_materialized or metrics.edge_materialization_duration_seconds, so there is no observability that the step is missing. Mitigating factors: graph layer is opt-in per request (enable_graph default False at app/schemas/pedr_search.py:187; include_graph_context default False), so default search results are unaffected; ingestion itself completes normally; graph_edges is derived data and a one-off `python -m app.cli.materialize_edges --full` against prod would backfill it once Stage 6 is restored. Classified high (feature silently gone) rather than critical because no source-of-truth data is wrong and nothing is a security regression.

confirmed.refuter_reasoning: Defaulting to is_behavior_change=false, I tried to show the import removal was a legitimate F401 autofix or that Stage 6 was moved/re-expressed. Both refutations fail. F401 only removes UNUSED imports; at 8b049eda4b the import is used at L406. Running ruff (I, UP, F401, SIM, B, unsafe fixes, plus format) with the repo's own pyproject config on the pre-commit file retains both the import and the 39-line Stage 6 block — so the deletion is not a ruff artifact; it is a manual (or non-ruff tooling) deletion, after which the import became dead and was stripped. The pre-commit path calls EdgeMaterializationService.materialize_implicit_edges and populates result["stages"]["edges_materialized"] + result["metrics"]; the post-commit path does neither — different observable results and different DB side effects (graph_edges rows). The claim's specific assertion — the import was the sole dependency of the deleted Stage 6 block and must be restored with it — is exactly correct. Blast radius is narrower than "graph layer off everywhere":
- UNAFFECTED: the primary PEDR search surface. POST /api/v1/pedr/search always passes `enable_graph=payload.enable_graph` (app/api/v1/pedr_search.py:149); `_merge_config` (search_orchestrator.py:908-912) honors that explicit override, so the PEDRConfig default is never consulted. UI users still get L6 expansion.
- AFFECTED: RAGService, the only prod consumer that relies on the PEDRConfig default. It builds its orchestrator via `create_pedr_orchestrator()` with no config (app/services/rag_service.py:161 -> `PEDRConfig()` at search_orchestrator.py:352) and calls `self.pedr_orchestrator.search(**search_kwargs)` without `enable_graph` (rag_service.py:427-451). GraphLayerService is auto-wired (`self.graph_service = graph_service or GraphLayerService()`), so pre-d592c92 the RAG retrieval path ran L6 graph candidate expansion; post-d592c92 the `if config.enable_graph and self.graph_service` gate (L710) is silently False. RAGService backs prod routes app/api/v1/search.py:45 (POST /search RAG query), saved_searches.py:207, and search_history.py:140 (re-run). Effect: degraded recall / answer context on the RAG /search path for queries that benefit from graph-expanded candidates. Not wrong data, not a security regression. RAG's separate GraphRAGHelper "graph context" mechanism (rag_service.py:202, :677-693, `include_graph_context`) is a different feature and is unaffected.
- Also affected (non-prod): scripts/pedr_benchmark.py:75 calls `orchestrator.search(query=..., top_k=...)` on defaults, so benchmark numbers measure a no-graph stack, contrary to the Sprint 34 T34.4 intent.

Context: the True default lived ~17 hours (aa32f9d 2026-03-12 17:50 -> d592c92 2026-03-13 10:43), so the Sprint 34 "Activate Graph Layer (L6)" deliverable effectively never reached production for its only real consumer (RAG defaults). Severity set to medium rather than high because the headline PEDR search API/UI retain graph expansion via explicit flags; it would be high if RAG-path L6 expansion is counted as a shipped feature, since for that path it is silently gone.

# --- Audit Logging ---


def _get_client_ip(request: Request) -> str:
    """Extract client IP, respecting X-Forwarded-For."""
    forwarded = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for")
    if forwarded:
        return forwarded.split(",")[0].strip()
    return request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"


def _log_auth_failure(request: Request, email: str, reason: str) -> None:
    """Log a failed authentication attempt with structured context.

    Logs IP and failure reason for security audit. Does NOT log passwords or
    other sensitive data.
    """
    ip = _get_client_ip(request)
    logger.warning(
        "auth_failure: ip=%s email=%s reason=%s",
        ip,
        email,
        reason,

def create_mission_from_draft(
        self,
        db: Session,
        *,
        project_id: UUID,
        draft: Union[MissionProtocolDraft, Dict[str, Any]],
        requested_status: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Mission:
        ...
        mapped_status = _map_protocol_status(status)

        # Extract objective from research_statement or summary
        objective = ""
        if draft.research_statement and draft.research_statement.objective:
            objective = draft.research_statement.objective
        elif draft.summary:
            objective = draft.summary
        else:
            objective = draft.title or f"Mission {draft.mission_id}"

        # Extract success criteria from key_questions
        success_criteria = []
        if draft.key_questions:
            success_criteria = [kq.question for kq in draft.key_questions if kq.question]
        if not success_criteria:
            success_criteria = ["Complete mission protocol"]

        quality_gates = self._merged_quality_gates(snapshot, None)
        protocol_data = draft.model_dump(mode="json")

        mission = Mission(
            project_id=project_id,
            mission_id=draft.mission_id,
            title=draft.title or f"Mission {draft.mission_id}",
            objective=objective,
            success_criteria=success_criteria,
            context=protocol_data,
            tags=draft.tags or [],
            status=mapped_status,
            execution_metadata={
                "quality_gates": quality_gates,
                "completion_percentage": snapshot.completion_percentage,
            },
        )
        db.add(mission)
        self._sync_evidence_links(db, draft)
        db.commit()
        db.refresh(mission)
        self._trigger_quality_automation(mission.id)
        mission_id_str = str(mission.id)
        self.cache_manager.invalidate_quality_gates(mission_id_str)
        self.cache_manager.invalidate_mission_validation(mission_id_str)
        return mission

refuted.description: d592c92 replaced `from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple` with `from typing import Any` plus `from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Sequence`, and modernized `Optional/Dict/List/Tuple` in the first ~660 lines — but the three T38.1 semantic-edge methods at the bottom of the file were left untouched and still reference the now-unimported names at post-commit lines 674, 675 (`project_id: Optional[str]`, `since: Optional[datetime]`), 698 (`collection_chunks: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}`), 739, 741, 744, 745 (`session: Optional[Session] = None`, `project_id: Optional[str] = None`, `qdrant_client: Optional[Any] = None`, `collection_name: Optional[str] = None`), 784, 787, 788, and 830 (`chunk_urn_map: Dict[str, str] = {}`). ruff F821 reports 12 undefined-name errors on the post file (0 on the pre file). Impact is static/typing only, not a runtime crash: the module has `from __future__ import annotations` so parameter annotations are lazy strings, and PEP 526 local-variable annotations are never evaluated — a probe confirmed defining and calling such a function succeeds, while `typing.get_type_hints()` on it raises NameError. Reported because it is the same import-removed-while-still-used pattern as the `Collection` finding, makes the module's annotations unresolvable for any introspection, and would fail lint (the repo enforces `ruff check`). Repaired by commit 065a452; HEAD is clean.
refuted.why_refuted: The claim is accurate in its facts but, by its own admission, is not a behavior change, and the diff confirms that: the Optional/Dict/List/Tuple references that d592c92 orphaned are all annotation-only. Under PEP 563 (`from __future__ import annotations`) function parameter annotations are stored as strings and never evaluated at def time; PEP 526 annotations on local variables inside a function body are never evaluated at all (the compiler does not even store them). The pre- and post-commit code paths for `_collection_cooccurrence_edges`, `materialize_topic_similarity_edges`, and `_topic_similarity_edge_specs` therefore execute identical bytecode for every statement that actually runs; the probe and the real module import both demonstrate this. The only observable difference is for tooling that resolves annotations (`typing.get_type_hints`, pydantic, FastAPI dependency injection), and no caller in the repo does that for these methods. So for the claimed symbols: is_behavior_change=false, severity none, lint-only debt repaired by 065a452. I am flagging, but not folding into this verdict, that the same hunk dropped the `Collection` model import while line 686 still executes `.join(Collection, ...)` at runtime -- that one is a genuine NameError on the `materialize_implicit_edges` path and is the distinct, already-reported "Collection finding" which the same repair commit fixed.
